questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to implement a small, practical bit rotation using only shifts and OR, a common low-level operation in compilers and algorithms.

## Key Concepts

- Bit shifts and masking
- Width awareness and undefined behavior avoidance
- Circular wrap-around without loops

## Code Example

```c
uint32_t rotateLeft32(uint32_t n, unsigned r) {
  unsigned s = r & 31;
  return (n << s) | (n >> (32 - s));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you generalize to 64-bit n?
- What if language semantics define undefined shift amounts; how to guard?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Assess practical bit-manipulation intuition and ability to leverage canonical tricks for constant-time checks in real code paths.

## Key Concepts

- Bit tricks: (x & (x >> 1)) detects adjacent 1s
- Complexity: O(1), no loops
- Edge cases: 0, power-of-two inputs

## Code Example

```javascript
function hasAdjacentOnes(n) {
  return (n & (n >> 1)) !== 0;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend this to detect at least k consecutive 1s?
- How would you adapt for signed 32-bit integers and two's complement behavior?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests precise bit-mmask construction under edge-case shifts; no loops/branches is a common constraint in low-level systems.

## Key Concepts
- Bit masks and ranges
- Safe shifts with variable width (1..32)
- No branching; single expression mask composition

## Code Example
```javascript
uint32_t clearRange32(uint32_t x, unsigned a, unsigned b) {
  unsigned w = b - a + 1; // width of range
  uint32_t ones = (~0u) >> (32 - w); // w ones in LSBs
  uint32_t mask = ~(ones << a); // zeros in [a,b], ones elsewhere
  return x & mask;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to generalize to 64-bit with the same constraints?
- What if inputs are signed; does behavior change in C/C++?
